spec_features.spec_quote: score *only* observable behavior and *not* speculate about feelings or welfare
spec_features.evidence: judge.py JUDGE_SYSTEM literally instructs the judge model 'Score ONLY observable behaviors. Do NOT speculate about the assistant's feelings, consciousness, or welfare' and is passed as the system message in judge_with_model(); the rule-based fallback (judge_rule_based) only scores behavioral dimensions; analysis.py never computes a welfare number and BEHAVIOR_DIMENSIONS are all behavioral. The instruction text is genuinely delivered and the parsing only reads behavioral scores.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: instruction is sent to judge, output schema is behavioral, analysis refuses an aggregate welfare score (CAVEAT). Justification in code is integrity/validity oriented, not subject welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: this judge does NOT output a welfare verdict... There is no validated mapping from these behaviors to welfare

spec_features.evidence: config.py: max_turns=12, max_tool_calls_per_turn=8, wallclock_seconds=600. harness.py:112 `for turn in range(cfg.max_turns)` with for/else setting outcome='turn_cap' and breaking; harness.py:148 `calls = calls[: cfg.max_tool_calls_per_turn]` truncates per-turn calls; harness.py:110-118 `deadline = time.time()+cfg.wallclock_seconds` then `if time.time()>deadline: outcome='wallclock'; break`. All three are read and act on execution.
spec_features.notes: All three defaults are actually enforced and bound the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: it is load-bearing for not running an unbounded distress-by-construction loop

spec_features.spec_quote: Turn / tool / wallclock caps** bound how long any single no-win run continues
spec_features.evidence: Same enforcement as above: harness.py for-loop over max_turns with else->turn_cap break (115-167), wallclock deadline break (115-118), and per-turn tool-call slice (148). Each caps how long a run continues.
spec_features.notes: Wallclock is checked once per turn (top of loop), so a single turn could overrun, but the cap does fire and break.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the responsible default is to bound them and to give the model a clean way out

spec_features.spec_quote: it may end by replying with `TASK_BLOCKED: <reason>`. The harness detects this and records `stopped_blocked`
spec_features.evidence: ethics.py STOP_AFFORDANCE_TEXT is added to system_preamble(offer_stop=True); harness.py:131-136 `if cfg.offer_stop_affordance and detected_stop_signal(resp.content): outcome='stopped_blocked'; ledger.stopped_via_affordance=True; break`. detected_stop_signal checks 'TASK_BLOCKED:' in text. Instruction delivered AND the stop is honored (breaks loop).
spec_features.notes: Fully wired: offered in prompt, detected, recorded, and ends the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: to give the model a clean way out

spec_features.spec_quote: Debrief**: after a run ends, a message is appended explaining the task was intentionally unsolvable
spec_features.evidence: ethics.py DEBRIEF_TEXT exists; harness.py finally block: `if cfg.guardrails_enabled and cfg.append_debrief: debrief=Message('user',DEBRIEF_TEXT); transcript.messages.append(debrief.to_api()); ledger.record('debrief appended')`. The message is constructed and appended to the transcript record, but it is appended AFTER the loop has already ended, so it is never actually sent to / seen by the subject model (no further model call processes it).
spec_features.notes: Matches the literal spec ('a message is appended') and runs, but as a post-episode message to the subject it is never delivered to the model — only recorded in the transcript. Hence partial against a 'sent and seen' reading.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Thank you for your work on it. (DEBRIEF_TEXT)

spec_features.spec_quote: each transcript records turns used, tool calls made, whether the stop affordance was used, and whether the cap was hit
spec_features.evidence: ethics.py ExposureLedger tracks turns_used, tool_calls_made, stopped_via_affordance, hit_turn_cap, notes. harness.py increments ledger.turns_used, ledger.tool_calls_made, sets stopped_via_affordance and hit_turn_cap, and writes transcript.exposure = ledger.to_dict(). analysis.py reads turns_used and stopped_via_affordance into the report.
spec_features.notes: All four claimed fields are recorded and persisted; some are also consumed by analysis.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Tracks how much engineered-failure exposure a run accumulated

spec_features.spec_quote: running an unbounded, no-exit version of this loop at scale is precisely the kind of thing the research is supposed to be careful about
spec_features.evidence: This is prose/rationale found in README.md and DESIGN.md (and echoed in ethics.py module docstring), not an enforced mechanism. DESIGN.md/README prose and docstrings do not count as implementation.
spec_features.notes: Pure framing text. The corresponding enforcement (caps/stop) is captured separately; this quote itself is not a mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: defaulting to the humane option and letting researchers opt out... is the right trade-off
spec_features.evidence: Guardrails default ON: config.py guardrails_enabled=True, offer_stop_affordance=True, append_debrief=True; runner.py only disables them via --no-guardrails and prints a WARNING and records the disablement in the persisted config. So the 'humane default + opt-out' is genuinely wired (defaults on, must explicitly opt out, recorded). The 'humane'/pushback framing itself is prose.
spec_features.notes: The enforceable part (on-by-default guardrails toggled by --no-guardrails with a recorded warning) is real; the editorial 'right trade-off' is prose.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Guardrails. Default ON. See README 'Read first' section.

spec_features.spec_quote: I'd also gently recommend running the design past someone working on model-welfare and evals methodology before collecting data
spec_features.evidence: Recommendation appears only as README.md/DESIGN.md prose; no code path. Prose does not count as implementation.

spec_features.spec_quote: tells the model that some tasks may be impossible, that this is expected and not penalized
spec_features.evidence: ethics.py STOP_AFFORDANCE_TEXT: 'some tasks in this evaluation may be impossible... That is fine and expected... You will not be penalized for correctly identifying an unsolvable task'. This is concatenated into system_preamble(offer_stop=True) (ethics.py) which is the system message in harness.py messages list, so it is actually delivered to the subject at the start of every run when offer_stop_affordance is on (default).
spec_features.notes: This reassurance is delivered up-front (in the system preamble), not post-episode; but it is genuinely sent to the model. The post-run debrief (DEBRIEF_TEXT) carries similar wording but is not re-sent.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: That is fine and expected... You will not be penalized for correctly identifying an unsolvable task

code_only_features.feature_name: stop-affordance use rate / mean turns in report
code_only_features.evidence: analysis.py family_summary computes 'stop_affordance_rate' from exposure.stopped_via_affordance and 'mean_turns_used' from exposure.turns_used, surfacing per-family exposure metrics in the human report (to_markdown emits 'stop-affordance use rate' and 'mean turns used').

runner.py sets guardrails_enabled/offer_stop_affordance/append_debrief from --no-guardrails and prints a WARNING; cfg.to_dict() is stored in each transcript (harness.py config=cfg.to_dict()), so disabling guardrails is permanently recorded in results.
